title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a very faint pencil sheet. It is written on the verso of the 1979 university letter, and its content is essentially the same as the next page (p.70). It is either a first faint draft or show-through, so the next page's transcription is the reliable reading.

**Setting.** The setting is the moduli spaces M_{0,K} of smooth genus-0 curves with marked points indexed by a finite set K. Over M_{0,K} there are line bundles L_i, one for each i in K: most plausibly the cotangent-line (psi) bundles at the marked points, taken on the open moduli space with the symmetric-group (G_K) equivariant structure. L_K := ⊗_{i∈K} L_i.

**Comparison formula.** For the forgetful map p_{K∖{i},K} : M_{0,K} → M_{0,K∖{i}}, Grothendieck writes L_i ≃ L_K ⊗ p^*L_{K∖{i}}.

**Why torsion is the issue.** The open M_{0,n} is a complement of hyperplanes in affine space, so its ordinary Picard group is 0. The nontrivial question is equivariant: the torsion of these bundles in Pic of the stack [M_{0,n}/S_n], i.e. in H^1(M_{0,I}, G_I·G_m). The latter is the group mentioned (crossed out) on p.70, and is essentially a group of characters of the genus-0 Teichmüller/mapping-class groups.

**The table** (n = 4, 5, 6) records:
- (n−1)(n−2) = 6, 12, 20;
- the 'best exponent to trivialize L': 3, 12?, 20?;
- the 'best exponent to trivialize L_i': 6, 12?, 60?.

So Grothendieck is computing the orders of these torsion classes. Only n = 4 is settled; n = 5 and 6 are conjectural (question marks).

**Inductive step for n = 5.** Take the product over 4-element subsets A ⊂ K of p_A^*(L_A). Each i lies in C(4,3) = 4 of these subsets, so the product equals (∏_{i∈K} L_i)^{⊗4} = L^4. Since L_A^{⊗3} is trivial for |A| = 4, it follows that (L^4)^3 is trivial. This bounds the order of L for n = 5 by 12, consistent with the guessed '12?'.

**Purpose.** The aim is to understand the character group / Picard torsion of the genus-0 modular towers. This is needed for the Teichmüller-groupoid programme, e.g. trivializing the central G_m-extensions and the 'Lego' gluing of M_{0,4} and M_{0,5}.
errors: No errors visible in what can be read.
The counting step (each i lies in 4 of the 4-subsets of a 5-set) is correct.
The step only yields an upper bound (12) on the order of L for n=5, as the question mark acknowledges.
The entries for n=5,6 are explicitly conjectural.
